headline: Chips Drag as Homebuilders Lead; Geopolitical Crosscurrents Set the Tone for the Week
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a broadly constructive note, with 294 of 501 names in our universe finishing higher. Homebuilders led all sectors, advancing 2.8%, while Software added 2.04% and Consumer edged up 0.8%. The day's tone was decisively split, however, as Semiconductors shed 4.92% — the sharpest sectoral decline — dragging on what was otherwise a resilient tape. Energy also softened, slipping 0.53% amid reports that China is quietly pushing for a negotiated end to the US-Iran conflict, which weighed on crude prices.

The session's standout mover was Schlumberger, surging 11.01% in a striking divergence from the broader energy sector's weakness. Packaging Corp rose 8.76% and VeriSign climbed 7.04%. On the other side of the ledger, MaxLinear plunged 21.54%, Bloom Energy fell 14.91%, and Hims & Hers Health dropped 14.20%, while Sandisk, Power Integrations, and Credo Technology each lost between roughly 10% and 11%.

Heading into the new week, investors face a dense geopolitical backdrop: the Iran conflict has extended to the Red Sea and Caspian Sea, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is expected in Washington, and Qualcomm has signaled double-digit price increases — a potential fresh catalyst for semiconductor volatility. Earnings and macro data will compete for attention against these headline risks.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Faces Another Test After Friday's Rout
briefs.body: The semiconductor group shed 4.92% on Friday, the worst sectoral performance in our universe, with MaxLinear collapsing 21.54%, Sandisk off 10.79%, Power Integrations down 10.46%, and Credo Technology losing 9.87%. Into the new week, Qualcomm's reported plan to raise prices by double digits could reinject volatility across the chip supply chain.

briefs.headline: Schlumberger's Double-Digit Surge Defies Broader Energy Weakness
briefs.body: Schlumberger surged 11.01% on Friday even as the broader energy sector fell 0.53% — a notable divergence that traders will be watching for follow-through. Oil prices came under pressure after reports emerged that China is lobbying for a negotiated end to the US-Iran war, cooling near-term supply-risk premiums.

briefs.headline: Iran Conflict Widens to New Waterways, Lifting Geopolitical Risk Premium
briefs.body: Fighting linked to the Iran war has spread to the Red Sea and the Caspian Sea, with Iran confirming a sailor was killed in what it described as a Ukrainian attack on a Caspian vessel. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately warned Britain would become a target if it backed US military action, broadening the diplomatic stakes heading into the week.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu Washington Visit Adds Mideast Diplomacy to the Calendar
briefs.body: President Trump announced that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu will travel to the United States next week, injecting a high-profile diplomatic event into a market week already freighted with geopolitical uncertainty. The meeting is likely to draw focus to ceasefire prospects and the trajectory of US engagement in the broader regional conflict.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders and Software Provide Shelter as Rotation Plays Out
briefs.body: With Homebuilders up 2.8% and Software gaining 2.04% on Friday, defensive-leaning growth names absorbed capital rotating out of semiconductors. Trimble and Samsara, up 5.08% and 5.14% respectively, exemplified the appetite for software and IoT names. Traders will watch whether this rotation extends or reverses as earnings season deepens.

briefs.headline: Anthropic Cost-Efficiency Move Shapes AI Infrastructure Debate
briefs.body: Anthropic's unveiling of a more cost-efficient model designed for everyday tasks arrives as a meaningful datapoint in the ongoing discussion about AI infrastructure spending. The development adds a new competitive variable for enterprise software buyers and cloud providers heading into a week when technology earnings remain a central market focus.
